sections.heading: Energy & power infrastructure — the grid view

blocks.text: (The generation story lives in E2-013/014; THIS note is the **infrastructure view** — wires, pipes, plants as assets.) blocks.text: India urbanises by ~1 crore people/yr toward **~40% urban by 2030 (600 mn)** — cities generating ~**60-65% of GDP on ~3% of land**. sections.heading: Weather forecasting & disaster management as infrastructure

blocks.text: (The science lives in ED-021/G-092; THIS note frames forecasting-DM as **infrastructure with finance-ownership-O&M questions**.) The asset stack: **IMD's observation network** (39 Doppler radars → 87 planned under **Mission Mausam (2024, ₹2,000 cr — 'weather-ready, climate-smart India')**, AWS/ARG thousands, INSAT-3DR/Oceansat satellites, HPC ~22 petaflops (Arka-Arunika era)), **INCOIS-NIOT's ocean arrays**, state EOCs-ICCCs, the **CAP-SACHET alert grid**, cyclone shelters (~2,000+ NCRMP-built east coast), embankments-saline bunds. **The infrastructure economics**: forecasting's benefit-cost runs ~1:50 (avoided losses) — the cheapest infrastructure India builds; ownership spans IMD-MoES (central), SDMA-district (state), panchayat (shelter O&M) — the classic **multi-level O&M orphanhood**: shelters decay between cyclones, radars need staffing, sirens need batteries.

rows: Finance
15th FC's mitigation-response funds (G-092); NCRMP's WB loans; Mission Mausam's capex; state SDRF shares — the shift from relief-spend to resilience-invest
Ownership clarity
Assets built centrally, owned locally, used episodically — MoUs and handover protocols the weak paper; community ownership (shelter-management committees with women's quotas) the working fix
**O&M discipline**

Shelter-maintenance funds (~₹1-2 lakh/shelter/yr needs), radar-technician cadres, drill calendars — 'disasters test maintenance, not construction'; **AP's practice — shelters doubling as schools-community halls (use keeps assets alive)** the model answer

items: **The framing move**: treat forecast-and-shelter as INFRASTRUCTURE CLASS — then finance (mitigation funds), ownership (community MoUs), O&M (use-based upkeep) become the answer's spine — precisely what this syllabus line uniquely asks versus the science notes.

**AP as the exhibit**: the zero-casualty doctrine is an O&M story — drilled communities, maintained shelters, staffed EOCs; Mission Mausam's radar densification includes the AP coast; the state's dual-use shelter practice is the national model.

blocks.text: **The issues file**: optimistic-bid winner's curse → renegotiation culture; land-clearance delays killing financial closure; **contract sanctity shocks (the AP PPA renegotiation 2019 — the national case study)**; dispute-resolution slowness (arbitration's award-challenge loops); banks' ALM mismatch funding 25-yr assets; and the **Kelkar Committee (2015)** prescription set — model-concession rebalancing, independent regulators, renegotiation frameworks (permitted for exogenous shocks, barred for bid-remorse), the proposed **infrastructure-PPP tribunal**.

items: **Pricing theory for utilities**: marginal-cost pricing vs average-cost recovery; **cross-subsidy** (industry overpaying for farm-domestic under-payment — power's AP file); lifeline blocks + volumetric beyond (water-power equity design); congestion pricing (roads' frontier); the **political-economy law — un-priced utilities decay** (free water = dry taps; the O&M funeral); the reform grammar: **price the service, subsidise the person (DBT), publish the subsidy**.

**Environmental impacts of infrastructure**: linear projects' fragmentation (roads through Eastern Ghats corridors — mitigation: eco-ducts, alignment shifts), ports' shoreline effects (PL-026's drift file), big dams' sediment-displacement double bill (Polavaram's R&R-ecology ledger), construction's dust-debris (C&D rules), transmission-vs-bustard (the GIB case) — the discipline: **EIA-and-mitigation as project cost, not obstacle** (ED-020), with cumulative-corridor assessment the reform.

**The synthesis**: PPP allocates risk, pricing allocates burden, EIA allocates externalities — infrastructure policy is allocation design three times over; AP's decade (PPA shock → HAM-era rebuild → landlord ports → Polavaram's ledger) supplies every exhibit.

blocks.text: Exam tip: 'Price the service, subsidise the person, publish the subsidy' — utility pricing's whole reform in nine words; and HAM as 'the renegotiated equilibrium' shows you understand PPP history, not just acronyms.

prelimsPointers: **HAM**: 40% construction support + annuity with traffic risk on NHAI — the post-2016 road-PPP standard.
**Kelkar Committee on PPPs (2015)**: rebalanced concessions, renegotiation framework, independent regulators, PPP-tribunal proposal.
**TOT** (toll-operate-transfer) and **InvITs** monetise operating assets — brownfield de-risked PPP.
**Landlord model**: public authority owns port-airport land; private concessions operate (Bhogapuram-GMR the AP case).
**Cross-subsidy surcharge** — industry's tariff premium funding under-priced categories in power.
**Lifeline block pricing** — free/cheap first units with rising volumetric rates: equity-efficiency design.
**GIB transmission case**: SC ordered undergrounding in bustard habitat (2021; modified 2024) — ecology pricing infrastructure.
The **2019 AP PPA renegotiation** remains the national contract-sanctity case study.
mainsAngles: Allocate risk to its best manager — evaluate India's PPP model evolution from BOT's burns to HAM's equilibrium.
Renegotiation needs rules, not remorse — apply the Kelkar framework to the contract-sanctity problem.
Un-priced utilities decay — argue the price-service-subsidise-person grammar with power and water.
Infrastructure's externalities are project costs — integrate EIA-mitigation and cumulative assessment into project economics.
Risk, burden, externality — three allocations, one infrastructure policy: synthesise with AP's decade of exhibits.

glossary.definition: The long-term contract allocating build-operate-revenue risks between authority and private partner — PPP's constitution.
Over-optimistic bids winning and then failing — the renegotiation culture's seed.
One consumer class overpaying to fund another's under-payment — power pricing's embedded transfer.
Subsidised basic-consumption block ensuring affordability while pricing excess use.
Capital grants (up to 20-40%) making socially desirable but commercially marginal PPPs bankable.
Corridor-basin level environmental evaluation beyond single projects — infrastructure EIA's reform frontier.
